scenes.tts: Which loses more of the cortex: an eye that sends nothing, or an eye that sends noise?
scenes.visual: Title card: Silence Is Not Noise. One dark eye, one eye with scattered spikes. Convention: left hemisphere recorded; right eye (contralateral) orange, left eye (ipsilateral) blue; histograms run group 1 on the left to group 7 on the right.
scenes.narration: Which loses more of the cortex: an eye that sends nothing, or an eye that sends noise?

scenes.tts: Lid suture blurs an eye's image. But its retina keeps firing under the lid.
scenes.visual: A sutured eye: blurred light gets through the lid; its retina still produces spikes.
scenes.narration: Lid suture blurs an eye's image. But its retina keeps firing under the lid.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-six, Michael Stryker's laboratory asked whether electrical activity itself is what counts.
scenes.caption: In 1986, Michael Stryker's laboratory asked whether electrical activity itself is what counts.
scenes.visual: Credit: Stryker laboratory, 1986 (Chapman and colleagues).
scenes.narration: In 1986, Michael Stryker's laboratory asked whether electrical activity itself is what counts.

scenes.tts: They silenced one eye of kittens with tetrodotoxin, a toxin that blocks sodium channels.
scenes.visual: A syringe labelled tetrodotoxin; sodium channels in the retina are plugged.
scenes.narration: They silenced one eye of kittens with tetrodotoxin, a toxin that blocks sodium channels.

scenes.tts: It silences the retinal ganglion cells, the eye's output neurons.
scenes.visual: The retinal ganglion cells of the injected eye go dark.
scenes.narration: It silences the retinal ganglion cells, the eye's output neurons.

scenes.tts: Cortical responses shifted toward the eye that kept firing.
scenes.visual: The histogram shifts toward the active eye. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Cortical responses shifted toward the eye that kept firing.

scenes.tts: So an imbalance of electrical activity between the eyes is enough to cause a shift.
scenes.visual: Label: an imbalance of electrical activity is enough.
scenes.narration: So an imbalance of electrical activity between the eyes is enough to cause a shift.

scenes.tts: In the same year, Stryker and William Harris silenced both eyes during development.
scenes.visual: Credit: Stryker and Harris, 1986. Both eyes dark.
scenes.narration: In the same year, Stryker and William Harris silenced both eyes during development.

scenes.tts: Then the two eyes' axons failed to separate into stripes.
scenes.visual: Layer 4: orange and blue endings stay intermixed instead of forming stripes.
scenes.narration: Then the two eyes' axons failed to separate into stripes.

scenes.tts: Now there are two ways to take an eye out of the contest.
scenes.visual: Two cards side by side: sutured eye, silenced eye.
scenes.narration: Now there are two ways to take an eye out of the contest.

scenes.tts: A sutured eye, whose retina still fires. And a silenced eye, which sends nothing at all.
scenes.visual: The sutured eye shows scattered, unpatterned spikes; the silenced eye shows a flat line.
scenes.narration: A sutured eye, whose retina still fires. And a silenced eye, which sends nothing at all.

scenes.tts: Predict. If the more active eye simply wins, which closed eye should lose more? What does our rule predict?
scenes.visual: Question card: sutured or silenced, which loses more? Two rules listed: more active wins; helps it fire.
scenes.narration: Predict. If the more active eye simply wins, which closed eye should lose more? What does our rule predict?

scenes.tts: By amount, the silenced eye is quieter, so it should lose more. It loses less.
scenes.visual: The silenced eye's bar shrinks a little; the sutured eye's bar shrinks more. Schematic.
scenes.narration: By amount, the silenced eye is quieter, so it should lose more. It loses less.

scenes.tts: In kittens, lid suture weakens the closed eye's responses more than tetrodotoxin does.
scenes.visual: Credit: Rittenhouse and colleagues, 1999. Label: suture weakens more than tetrodotoxin.
scenes.narration: In kittens, lid suture weakens the closed eye's responses more than tetrodotoxin does.

scenes.tts: Why? The sutured eye's retina is still active under the lid.
scenes.visual: The sutured eye's spikes play under the lid.
scenes.narration: Why? The sutured eye's retina is still active under the lid.

scenes.tts: That leftover activity is unpatterned. It is out of step with the cells it drives.
scenes.visual: Its spikes are scattered against the cortical cell's firing, which follows the open eye.
scenes.narration: That leftover activity is unpatterned. It is out of step with the cells it drives.

scenes.tts: And it seems to weaken the eye's own synapses.
scenes.visual: The sutured eye's synapses on the cell thin.
scenes.narration: And it seems to weaken the eye's own synapses.

scenes.tts: A silent eye is never active at the wrong moments. So it loses less.
scenes.visual: The silenced eye's synapse shrinks less than the sutured eye's.
scenes.narration: A silent eye is never active at the wrong moments. So it loses less.

scenes.tts: So the rule that the more active eye wins fails this test. So does simple disuse.
scenes.visual: The card more active wins is crossed out.
scenes.narration: So the rule that the more active eye wins fails this test. So does simple disuse.

scenes.tts: The rule in the box can account for the difference. The sutured eye's input is the kind its weakening half acts on; a silent input is left nearly alone.
scenes.visual: Rule card: the cell keeps the eye that helps it fire, with its second half highlighted.
scenes.narration: The rule in the box can account for the difference. The sutured eye's input is the kind its weakening half acts on; a silent input is left nearly alone.

scenes.tts: The open eye drives the cell's strong responses. On its own, the sutured eye evokes only weak ones.
scenes.visual: Timeline: the cell's strong responses follow the open eye; the sutured eye's spikes, alone, push the response meter only below the threshold line.
scenes.narration: The open eye drives the cell's strong responses. On its own, the sutured eye evokes only weak ones.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: silence is not the same as noise. An eye whose activity is out of step with the cell loses more than an eye that is simply silent.
scenes.visual: Closing card: silence is not noise.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: silence is not the same as noise. An eye whose activity is out of step with the cell loses more than an eye that is simply silent.

scenes.tts: One question remains. Why does all of this work mainly in the young?
scenes.visual: A kitten beside an adult cat, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: One question remains. Why does all of this work mainly in the young?
